title: Two Buttons pass a bare `disabled` and go silent, against Button's own contract
body:
## Summary
Button promises "a disabled control is never silent" through `disabledReason`, but its Props still accept a bare `disabled` via `...rest`, and two callers use it with no reason.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/components/Button.tsx:33 renders `disabled={Boolean(disabledReason)} {...rest}`, so a caller's own `disabled` overrides the reason path and the wrapper that carries the reason is never drawn. apps/desktop/src/scenes/shared/EngineSection.tsx:84 (`disabled={model.checking}`) and apps/desktop/src/scenes/waking/view.tsx:143 (`disabled={url.trim() === ""}`) do exactly that: a disabled button with no title, no focus stop and no stated reason (house style 2.2, CATALOG.md's Button row). Technique: ui-controls/composition-contracts (a consumer prop silently disarms the primitive's guard). Fixed looks like: `disabled` removed from Button's Props so only `disabledReason` can disable, and the two callers say why ("Checking the engines…", "Type an address first.").

## Flow
- Open the first act's address step with an empty field -> waking/view.tsx:143 renders `<Button disabled>` -> the Open button is dimmed with no reason reachable by pointer or keyboard
- Press Check again in an engine section -> EngineSection.tsx:84 disables it while checking -> same, silent
- Fix in build order: Omit<…, "className" | "disabled"> in Button.tsx; give the two callers a disabledReason; add a source guard

## Expected impact
A keyboard or screen-reader user learns why two buttons are dead instead of finding a control that does nothing. Could break: a form submit button wrapped in the reason span still submits on Enter from the field only when enabled, which is the intent; check waking's submit path.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every disabled Button states its reason
Before: 2 Button call sites disable with no reason (grep `<Button` ... `disabled=` without disabledReason)
After: 0, predicted; not built: both sites are in scenes/, outside this round's paths
Method: probe - the grep on the real tree; the fix's figure needs the out-of-scope edit
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/components/Button.tsx:33  <button ... disabled={Boolean(disabledReason)} {...rest}>
apps/desktop/src/scenes/shared/EngineSection.tsx:84  <Button size="sm" onClick={model.actions.checkEngines} disabled={model.checking}>
apps/desktop/src/scenes/waking/view.tsx:143  <Button variant="primary" size="sm" type="submit" disabled={url.trim() === ""}>
instrument: Omit "disabled" from Button's Props: `pnpm typecheck` error count is the Before (2 sites), then give both callers a disabledReason and re-run (0); plus a source guard that no `<Button` in src passes `disabled=`.

title: Button's disabled-reason wrapper names a role-less span, so a reader hears the reason, not the control
body:
## Summary
With `disabledReason`, Button puts a focusable `<span tabIndex=0 aria-label={reason}>` around a natively disabled button; the span has no role, so ARIA prohibits its name, and where a reader does voice it, the reason replaces which button this is.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/components/Button.tsx:39 wraps the disabled button in `<span tabIndex={0} title={disabledReason} aria-label={disabledReason}>`. A `span` is role generic, on which aria-label is prohibited (ARIA 1.2), so NVDA/JAWS may announce nothing for the focus stop; where Chromium does expose the label, the user hears "Paste the token first." and never the button's own words ("Save"). Technique: accessibility/name-and-description-wiring (the reason is a description, the label is the name) and primitive-level-a11y (fix it once in the primitive). Fixed looks like: no wrapper; the button stays focusable with `aria-disabled="true"`, its click is suppressed while disabled, and the reason is its description (aria-describedby to a visually hidden node or the title). The `.field__row > span` rules (apps/desktop/src/styles/app.css:585-590) and motion-tokens.test.ts's pin of them go with the wrapper.

## Flow
- Tab to the Add button of accounts' recipient field while the draft is empty (scenes/accounts/view.tsx:485, disabledReason set) -> focus lands on the wrapper span -> a reader voices the reason or nothing, never "Add"
- Fix in build order: test on name/description -> Button renders aria-disabled + describedby -> CSS `.btn:disabled` selectors also match `[aria-disabled="true"]` -> drop `.field__row > span` rules and their pin

## Expected impact
Every disabled Button with a reason (23 importers of Button, about ten pass disabledReason) becomes one focus stop that says what it is and why it waits. Could break: callers that rely on the native disabled to block submit; the wrapper's layout in `.field__row`.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a disabled button is announced by its own name with the reason as its description
Before: 1 focus stop per disabled Button, role generic, aria-label = reason (Button.tsx:39)
After: predicted: the button itself, name = label, description = reason; not measured
Method: simulation - walked the accounts Add field and the Notion token Save; the instrument (an accessible-name test) is named and unbuilt; M across CSS, a pinned test and every caller's disabled styling
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/components/Button.tsx:33-41
  <button ... disabled={Boolean(disabledReason)} {...rest}>
  ...
  <span tabIndex={0} title={disabledReason} aria-label={disabledReason} className="focus-ring">
apps/desktop/src/styles/app.css:585 .field__row > span { display: flex; }
apps/desktop/src/styles/motion-tokens.test.ts:95-96 pin `.field__row > span`
instrument: A jsdom test computing the accessible name and description (dom-accessibility-api, already a transitive dep of testing tools, or a hand-rolled check of role/aria attributes) of a Button with disabledReason: Before = focus stop is a generic span whose aria-label replaces the button's name; After = the focus stop is the button itself (aria-disabled, aria-describedby the reason), name = its label.

title: A value rail's unavailable option, or a whole disabled rail, states its reason only on hover
body:
## Summary
PillGroup's `disabledReason` is a `title` on a natively disabled button, and a `disabled` group has no reason at all, so neither is reachable by keyboard or screen reader.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/components/PillGroup.tsx:87-88 sets `disabled={disabled || Boolean(option.disabledReason)}` and `title={option.disabledReason ?? option.hint}`. The PillOption doc says the reason "is shown, never merely implied", but a disabled button takes no focus, so the title is a mouse-only tooltip, and the arrows now step over it (commit ac4d17f). The group-level `disabled` (used by scenes/accounts/view.tsx:252 and :390 while a connector is busy) disables every pill with no reason anywhere. Technique: accessibility/hidden-but-mounted-inertness and name-and-description-wiring; ui-controls/micro-interaction-contracts. Fixed looks like: an unavailable option stays focusable with aria-disabled and its reason as description, and the group takes a `disabledReason` the way Button does.

## Flow
- Accounts -> a connector row while it is busy -> its on/off rail is disabled -> Tab skips it and nothing says it is busy
- Fix in build order: test -> aria-disabled pills that refuse the pick -> group-level disabledReason -> the two accounts callers pass `${row.busy}…`

## Expected impact
A keyboard user hears why a switch will not move instead of finding it missing from the tab order. Could break: the arrow walk now skips disabled pills; with aria-disabled it would need to land on them and refuse the pick.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an unavailable choice says why, by keyboard too
Before: 0 of 2 disabled states expose a reason to the keyboard (PillGroup.tsx:87-88)
After: predicted 2 of 2; the group-level reason needs scenes/accounts changes (out of scope)
Method: simulation - walked the accounts busy switch and a hypothetical uninstalled Whisper model; the test is named, unbuilt
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: jsdom test: a PillGroup with one option carrying disabledReason, and one with disabled; assert the reason is reachable by keyboard (focusable via aria-disabled, aria-describedby) - Before 0 of 2, After 2 of 2.

title: WindowControls reads two stores and IPC from src/components, which the catalog forbids
body:
## Summary
CATALOG.md rule 3 says src/components stays free of store and IPC imports ("a primitive that reads a store is a view"); WindowControls imports useSettings, useShell and hasShell and calls Tauri's window API itself.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/components/WindowControls.tsx:14-18 import `@tauri-apps/api/window`, `@/lib/ipc`, `@/stores/settings` and `@/stores/shell`; it has one caller, apps/desktop/src/console/Console.tsx:82 (CATALOG rule 1: two callers, or it stays in the module). It is a view of the stage's bar living in the primitives folder, and the rule that says so has no check. Technique: ui-controls/control-inventory-and-discovery (placement rules keep the catalog trustable). Fixed looks like: either WindowControls moves to console/ (its one caller) and leaves the catalog, or it takes `theme`, `onTheme` and the three window actions as props from Console; then a guard forbids store/IPC imports under src/components.

## Flow
- grep `@/stores/|@/lib/ipc` under src/components -> WindowControls.tsx only
- Fix in build order: guard test (red on WindowControls) -> move or prop-drive it (touches console/Console.tsx) -> guard green

## Expected impact
The primitives folder stays renderable without a shell or stores (the preview harness and tests stop mocking Tauri for it). Could break: Console's bar if the props are wired wrong; covered by the new WindowControls.test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the catalog's placement rule holds by test
Before: 1 of 10 primitives imports stores/IPC; 0 tests check rule 3
After: 0 of 10, 1 test; not built: the change needs console/Console.tsx, another context's file
Method: probe - grep on the real tree for the Before; the After needs the out-of-scope edit
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: A source guard in components/catalog.test.ts: no file in src/components imports `@/stores/` or `@/lib/ipc` - Before 1 file (WindowControls.tsx), After 0, once the component takes theme and window actions as props (or moves beside console/Console.tsx, its one caller).

title: The close confirm replaces the close button in one frame and widens the bar with no ease
body:
## Summary
Pressing close while a decision waits swaps the 40px close button for a ~260px confirm in one frame, shoving the bar's right end, and Keep swaps it back the same way.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/components/WindowControls.tsx:94 renders `confirming ? <span className="close-confirm">… : <button …close>`; `.close-confirm` (apps/desktop/src/styles/app.css, the close-confirm block) has no enter or exit, so the bar's trailing slot jumps in width. The overlay asks for state swaps to ease on transform/opacity and for enter with exit; motion technique continuity-across-change. This is a design and window call: the confirm only draws with a shell (hasShell), so the preview harness cannot show it, and keyed mount state for the exit is the same class as the restart notice in backlog-2026-10-13.

## Flow
- Main with a card waiting -> click close -> the confirm appears in one frame and the breadcrumb/bar content to its left reflows
- Keep -> it vanishes in one frame

## Expected impact
The one destructive question in the bar arrives calmly instead of jolting the layout. Needs the real Tauri window and, likely, the perf gate.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the confirm eases in and out without shifting the bar
Before: 0 ms enter, 0 ms exit, width jump of the trailing slot (read from the CSS; not seen)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - read from CSS and component; the window is the only place it renders
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/components/WindowControls.tsx:94  {confirming ? ( <span className="close-confirm" role="alertdialog" …> … ) : ( <button … window-btn--close …> )}
apps/desktop/src/components/WindowControls.tsx:70  if (!hasShell()) return null;
